lines: Washing your hair more often damages it.
That's what the internet says.
A 2021 study actually tested it.
People washed once a week, or every single day.
Daily washing came out ahead on every measure.
And no damage to the hair was found.
Two catches.
A shampoo company paid for the study,
and it didn't study curly or coily hair.
For tightly coiled hair, the American Academy of Dermatology suggests washing every week or two.
So wash when your scalp needs it,
not to follow a rule.
So, does washing more damage your hair?
Your hair floated in a glass of water?
That tells you nothing.
No study has shown the float test measures porosity.
Here's what labs do measure.
Porosity follows damage.
In one study, bleach nearly tripled the hair's surface area
in the first minute.
Damage opens up the hair.
So porosity isn't set by your curl type.
4C hair can be low, normal or high porosity.
Bleached or heat-damaged hair? Treat it as more porous.
And skip the glass of water.
Oil doesn't moisturize your hair.
Water does.
In a lab study, an oil film cut how much water hair took in,
but it also slowed water leaving.
So put your water-based product on first,
and your oil last, to seal it in.
And not every oil gets inside the hair.
Coconut oil got in.
Mineral oil stayed on the surface.
Jojoba, avocado, almond?
Never tested.
So which oil are you using?
Castor oil makes your hair grow?
Here's the catch.
No study has tested castor oil on its own for hair growth in people.
The growth idea comes from a lab theory:
that it may block a scalp chemical linked to pattern hair loss.
A 2026 dermatology review says that's still unproven.
What it can do: add shine.
And with heavy use, there are rare reports of hair felting,
strands matting into a hard tangle.
So if your hair isn't getting longer, look at breakage first.
So, does castor oil grow hair?
Your hair isn't stuck. It's breaking.
In a small case report, three people with tightly coiled hair combed it every day.
Three years after a haircut, their hair was only about seven centimeters long.
That's under three inches.
The hair was growing the whole time.
Daily combing acted like a daily haircut.
It's only three people, so it's a clue, not proof.
But it fits what we see: hair grows every month. Breakage is why length doesn't show.
Detangle wet, with conditioner in, starting at the ends.
And comb less often.
So, is your hair really not growing?
